entries.reason: MetalKit's own header declares it and forbids it: MTKModel.h:188 reads `- (nonnull instancetype)init NS_UNAVAILABLE;` with the words "Cannot use default init.  Must initialize with mesh and metal device", so no application compiled against it can call this. Apple's own class does not define it either, which was measured rather than read off the header: class_getInstanceMethod(MTLMesh.class, @selector(init)) answers, and its IMP is NSObject's own, the same one the superclass carries
entries.effect: the selector is not in the port's class: an MTKMesh is made by -initWithMesh:device:error:, which answers nil with an NSError in MTKModelErrorDomain saying this port does not carry MDLMesh (facts/MetalKit/TextureLoader.md). A caller that sends init anyway gets NSObject's, exactly as it would from Apple's class
entries.source: SDK 26.2, MetalKit, MTKModel.h:188; and Apple's own MetalKit, measured with class_getInstanceMethod and a nonsense-class control on tests/backports/host/metal-census

entries.reason: MTKModel.h:128 declares it NS_UNAVAILABLE with "Applicatiohs must not explicity allocate or initialize.  Must initialize as part of MTKMesh object", and Apple's own MTKSubmesh carries NSObject's init rather than one of its own, measured the same way as MTKMesh's
entries.effect: the selector is not in the port's class; a submesh is made by its mesh, and a caller that sends init anyway gets NSObject's
